//: Declared merge-policy target state across the active Goldberry-Playground repos (GOL-1819).
//gate: Ruleset and branch-protection WRITES are board-gated and not agent-executable (same class as GOL-392 / GOL-1207). scripts/ci/apply-merge-policy.sh --check is safe for anyone; --apply is Josh-only and needs an admin token. This file is the single source of truth so future drift is a diff, not archaeology.
//systems: GitHub unions two policy systems. 'ruleset' repos carry the settings in their named repository ruleset; 'legacy' repos carry them in classic branch protection on 'branch'. The script maps the canonical target keys below to the right API surface per system.
//fields: Canonical target keys (a key that is absent for a repo is NOT managed there): strict = require branch up-to-date with base (ruleset required_status_checks.strict_required_status_checks_policy | legacy required_status_checks.strict); dismiss_stale_reviews = dismiss approvals on push (ruleset pull_request.dismiss_stale_reviews_on_push | legacy required_pull_request_reviews.dismiss_stale_reviews); thread_resolution = require all review threads resolved (ruleset pull_request.required_review_thread_resolution | legacy required_conversation_resolution); extra_approval_unattributed = require a second approval for unattributed commits (ruleset pull_request.require_extra_approval_for_unattributed_changes | legacy: n/a).
//required_contexts: GOL-1953: the full required status-check context set for the branch (ruleset required_status_checks.required_status_checks[] | legacy required_status_checks.checks[]). This is the DECLARED TARGET — the guard layer (config-freeze / fix-touches-test / CI scripts / required-checks-audit + per-repo security checks) is promoted from advisory to branch-binding here. EVERY listed context was verified to report success on an actual merge_group commit first (acceptance #1) — a context whose job is skipped/conditional on merge_group (e.g. AgenticOS 'Dependency review', gated by a pull_request-only preflight) is DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED because it would wedge the merge queue. On --apply, legacy new contexts inherit the app_id shared by existing checks (15368 = GitHub Actions) and existing pins are preserved (never loosened); ruleset entries preserve any integration_id. LOCKSTEP: this list must equal the same repo's .github/required-checks.json (GOL-1907's reconcile leg hard-fails on declared-vs-live drift). Apply a repo (`--apply --repo X`) in the same batch as that repo's required-checks.json bump so a weekly reconcile never sees a mismatch. For a repo whose promotion PR has not landed yet, --check will show this as pending drift — expected, not a failure.
//guard-hold: GOL-2013 (board 2026-09-01, supersedes the GOL-1953 guard-hold): the 'Protected paths guard' workflow was REMOVED from all repos. It was never a required check here, and the only non-duplicate thing it did — SHA-binding an approval to the head commit so approve-then-push could not slip a change past review — is now done natively by branch protection's `dismiss_stale_reviews_on_push`. So it is no longer a promotion candidate and must NOT be re-added to any required_contexts set below. SEQUENCING DEFECT (found 2026-09-07): the guard removal shipped in all three repos that carried it (grove-sites #667, grove-odoo-modules #167, odoocker-goldberrygrove #600) while `dismiss_stale_reviews` was still declared AND live `false` in each — so the approve-then-push window this directive said was covered natively was in fact covered by nothing from the moment each of those PRs merged. This change flips the declared target to `true` for exactly those three (AgenticOS is handled in #666, and is already live true from the GOL-2049 migration). It does NOT become live until Josh converges each repo; until then --check reports it as drift, which is the point. AgriforestryOS is deliberately NOT flipped: it never carried the guard or the auto-approve carve-out, so there is no removed protection to replace there and turning this on would be a new policy decision, not a restoration. `scripts/ci/merge-policy-guard-replacement.test.mjs` holds this invariant so a future removal cannot again ship without its replacement. The rest of the list (config-freeze / fix-touches-test / CI scripts / required-checks-audit + per-repo security checks) genuinely runs and reports on merge_group and gates for real.
//sequencing: GOL-1953 sequencing, re-read 2026-10-14: GOL-1958 (missing-check sweep) LANDED and runs on every repo ('Sweep open PRs for required checks that never started' is present on recent merge_group commits), GOL-1954 (agent-review mirror) landed, and the Protected paths guard is gone (see //guard-hold) so the 2026-09-01 board STOP's only open question is moot. Every required_contexts entry below was RE-VERIFIED on 2026-10-14 against the last 7-12 real merge_group commits per repo (paginated check-runs, no context absent on any commit, every one reporting success). This file is still the declared TARGET only; nothing becomes live until `apply-merge-policy.sh --apply --surface protection --repo X` is run, board-gated, in the SAME batch as that repo's required-checks.json bump.
//out-of-scope: Not changed by this policy: required_approving_review_count. The merge-queue rulesets WERE out of scope until GOL-3051; see //merge_queue.
//agent-ops: GOL-2016 (CEO decision 2026-10-14, Option 2): a repo entry may carry `agent_ops: "out-of-scope"`. It means the repo is deliberately NOT on the agent pipeline: no github-sync bridge, no `agent-review/*` check-run, none of the six agent-ops workflows (auto-approve / ci-autofix / ci-failure-router / config-freeze / fix-touches-test / protected-paths-guard), and a human (Josh) reviews and merges by hand. Its `system` / `targets` / `required_contexts` are STILL managed here — those gate the repo's own CI, not the agent stack — so apply-merge-policy.sh treats the entry exactly as before; the key is a marker for people and sweeps. A CI-port sweep MUST skip agent-ops workflows for any repo carrying this key (the self-contained `required-checks-audit.yml` is fine). Reversible: if development resumes, register a github-sync bridge first, then port the six workflows in their current (post-GOL-1938 / GOL-1991) shape, then delete the key.
//merge_queue: GOL-3051: merge-queue settings live in each repo's own `merge-queue` ruleset, not in branch protection, so they are a SECOND managed surface (see `merge_queue_ruleset_name` + per-repo `merge_queue_targets`). Target keys are the raw GitHub `merge_queue` rule parameter names and only the declared ones are touched — merge_method / grouping_strategy / the entry-count knobs are carried through verbatim on --apply. WHY check_response_timeout_minutes = 90: all six repos shipped with GitHub's 30, which is SHORTER than the observed hosted-runner queue wait under ordinary multi-agent PR load (45–90 min measured on AgenticOS 2026-10-05). When the wait exceeds the timeout the queue is not slow, it is non-functional, and silently so: GitHub removes the entry, nothing turns red, the PR reverts to open + APPROVED + CLEAN, and the next agent re-enqueues and deepens the backlog (PR #814 dequeued 31m50s after enqueue with its required `CI` run still `queued`). 90 covers the worst wait actually observed. Same board gate as everything else here: --apply is Josh-only.

repos.//migration: GOL-2049 migrated this repo from classic branch protection to the `main-branch-protection` ruleset (id 22343539). The declared system was left at 'legacy', so apply-merge-policy.sh queried the classic API, got 404 Branch not protected, and hard-failed on the FIRST repo — taking the whole tool down. Repointed to the ruleset surface here. dismiss_stale_reviews is declared true because the migration set it true and GOL-2013 depends on it: it is the native replacement for the removed protected-paths guard's SHA-binding.

Re-introduce that set here IN THE SAME PR as `apply-merge-policy.sh --apply --repo AgenticOS` so declared==live==applied at all times.
